records.description: Cloud CRM and business platform with sales, service, marketing, commerce, and data products.
records.self_serve_details: A free Developer Edition org is documented for testing/development. API use requires the API Enabled permission and an OAuth client app configured within the org; this does not establish free production API access for every customer plan.

credential_access.path: Create/use a Salesforce org, enable API permission for the user, and configure an external client app/OAuth flow in that org.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Free Developer Edition is available for test/development; production org edition, user permissions, and org setup still govern access.

api.details: Official REST API supports create/manipulate/search of Salesforce records and access to query results, metadata, and other resources; Bulk, Metadata, and Connect REST APIs cover additional jobs. No endpoint count estimated.

mcp.details: First-party Salesforce DX MCP Server (beta) and Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers are listed in Salesforce developer documentation. These connect agents to an org/platform; this is distinct from a generic MCP wrapper.
mcp.search_scope: Official Salesforce developer MCP-solutions page and linked first-party server references inspected.

buildability.blocker: Org-scoped OAuth/client-app setup and API permission; production access depends on the target org and plan.
buildability.rationale: A documented REST API, OAuth flow, free test/developer org path, and official MCP options make an integration technically feasible. Org-specific credentials/permissions and production edition access prevent treating it as universally frictionless.

evidence.claim: Salesforce positions the product as a CRM suite with Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud and Commerce Cloud.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official CRM page lists Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud and Commerce Cloud products.

evidence.claim: Salesforce Connect REST quick start instructs developers to create an external client app, enable OAuth and connect with OAuth to obtain an access token.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Page outlines OAuth setup and obtaining/passing an access token.

evidence.claim: REST API requests operate with access tokens; REST API is an HTTP interface for records, queries and metadata.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: REST API docs describe Salesforce access through HTTP requests to resources; quick-start documents OAuth token flow.

evidence.claim: Developer Edition is free for testing/development; user profile needs API Enabled permission.
evidence.source_title: Step One: Sign up for Salesforce Developer Edition
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The page calls Developer Edition a free testing/development solution and notes the API Enabled user permission.

evidence.claim: API access requires an org/user permission and an org-configured client app, so a free test org is not proof of free production access.
evidence.source_title: Step One: Sign up for Salesforce Developer Edition
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Developer Edition instructions require API Enabled permission; authorization setup is configured in a Salesforce org.

evidence.claim: Salesforce REST API supports data create/manipulation/search and access to records, query results and metadata; additional APIs support other functions.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The official overview describes REST resources, records, query results, metadata, and related Bulk/Metadata/Connect APIs.

evidence.claim: Salesforce officially lists Salesforce DX MCP Server and Hosted MCP Servers.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: First-party Salesforce MCP solutions table includes Salesforce DX MCP Server (beta) and Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers.

evidence.claim: OAuth/API setup and org permissions are material build constraints despite a documented test org and first-party MCP offerings.
evidence.source_title: Step One: Sign up for Salesforce Developer Edition
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Free Developer Edition is for testing/development and requires API Enabled permission; combine with org-scoped OAuth setup.

limitations: A direct Salesforce OAuth deep-link tried during source discovery returned 404; the current Quick Start and REST API guide were used instead.
This is a public-documentation assessment; no Salesforce org was created or tested.
records.researcher_notes: Pilot sample selected to test OAuth, free developer org vs customer-org access, and first-party MCP discovery.

records.description: Cloud communications platform with APIs for messaging, voice, and email.
records.self_serve_details: Twilio documents free-trial signup without a credit card after email and phone verification. Trial includes limited product units, a 30-day expiry, and account-status restrictions; paid upgrade is needed to remove trial limits.

credential_access.path: Create a Twilio account, verify email and phone, then view Account SID/Auth Token in Console or create API keys.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Free trial credentials are available; trial usage and recipient/geographic/content restrictions apply, with paid upgrade to remove restrictions.

api.details: Multi-product HTTP APIs and SDK/CLI support; official Twilio documentation describes a hosted docs MCP indexing public API specifications across products. API breadth is broad across communications products; no endpoint count is used in this record.

mcp.details: First-party hosted Twilio MCP at https://mcp.twilio.com/docs. It searches/retrieves API docs and schemas (read-only); it does not execute Twilio API operations and needs no Twilio credentials.
mcp.search_scope: Official Twilio AI/MCP documentation inspected, including features, indexed material, auth and limitations.

buildability.blocker: Trial unit, recipient, geographic, template, and expiry restrictions; production sending requires paid account/upgrade.
buildability.rationale: A documented HTTP API, API-key/Basic auth, and self-serve free trial make integration feasible. Trial limits are material for a live communications agent, and the first-party MCP is documentation-only rather than an execution server.

evidence.claim: Twilio presents itself as APIs for SMS, email and voice.
evidence.source_title: Conversational AI and APIs for SMS, Email, Voice | Twilio
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official product page title and landing content describe APIs for SMS, Email and Voice.

evidence.claim: Twilio REST API requests use HTTP Basic authentication with an API key SID/secret; Account SID/Auth Token are a documented alternative for specified APIs.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The authentication section says API key SID and secret are used as Basic auth credentials; account SID/Auth Token are also documented.

evidence.claim: A free trial can be created without a credit card; trial credentials appear in Console; trial expires after 30 days and has product-specific restrictions.
evidence.source_title: Get started with your Twilio free trial account
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Page documents no-card signup, email/phone verification, trial credentials, free units and 30-day expiration.

evidence.claim: Console exposes Account SID/Auth Token and supports API-key management after self-serve signup.
evidence.source_title: Get started with your Twilio free trial account
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The trial guide says credentials can be viewed in Console; trial restrictions are enforced by account status.

evidence.claim: Twilio supports raw HTTP requests, SDKs and CLI; APIs are documented and multi-product.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The docs describe HTTP requests, Twilio SDKs, CLI, and webhooks in the API request guide.

evidence.claim: Twilio official docs MCP indexes public API specs and docs; it is read-only search/retrieval and does not execute API calls.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The documentation lists the public specs indexed and explicitly says the server is read-only and does not execute API calls.

evidence.claim: Twilio publicly documents a first-party hosted MCP endpoint with no account/auth required.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Hosted URL mcp.twilio.com/docs; no authentication; two tools search and retrieve API docs/schemas.

evidence.claim: Self-serve trial credentials support development, but trial limits block unrestricted production messaging; docs MCP is not an execution interface.
evidence.source_title: Get started with your Twilio free trial account
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The trial page lists usage/recipient/geo/content restrictions and paid upgrade path; combine with API docs.

evidence.claim: The first-party MCP is a docs/schema retrieval tool and not an API execution server.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official limitations state read-only and public specs only.

limitations: No Twilio account was created; signup and trial controls were verified from public docs only.
MCP availability is documented as Public Beta and may change.
records.researcher_notes: Pilot tests API key + Basic combination and distinguishes Twilio docs MCP from an action-capable MCP.

records.description: REST-based seller/vendor APIs for catalog, listings, pricing, orders, fulfillment, inventory, reporting and related selling operations.
records.self_serve_details: For a public app serving multiple sellers/vendors, official onboarding requires a developer profile review, approved roles and Amazon approval/listing for Selling Partner Appstore distribution. A private app for one organization follows a less public path; this distinction is material.

credential_access.path: Public developer registers through Solution Provider Portal, submits a developer profile/use case/security details, receives approval for roles, then registers a production app; each selling partner authorizes via LWA/OAuth.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Amazon review/approval and role qualification for public integration; seller/vendor authorization is required. Private internal applications have a separate route.

api.details: Official docs describe REST-based APIs across catalog/listings/pricing/orders/fulfillment/inventory, notifications and bulk operations; Data Kiosk supports GraphQL queries. Roles and access vary by operation.

mcp.details: No first-party MCP status assigned in the pilot first pass; targeted official-source MCP search is required before classifying absence.
mcp.search_scope: Incomplete in first pass; not evidence of no MCP.

buildability.blocker: Public developer profile/role approval and Amazon approval for public Appstore distribution; selling partners must separately authorize.
buildability.rationale: SP-API is broad and technically buildable, but a reusable public toolkit needs the approved public-developer/app route and role access. A private developer route is documented for one organization and does not remove the public distribution gate.

evidence.claim: SP-API is a REST-based API collection for seller/vendor operations such as orders, shipment tracking and payments.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official overview describes REST-based API and examples of seller/vendor workflows.

evidence.claim: Public-app authorization uses Login with Amazon OAuth 2.0; LWA access tokens are sent with SP-API requests.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The guide identifies LWA as OAuth 2.0 and documents code-to-refresh-token workflow; SP-API requests use access tokens.

evidence.claim: Public developers must complete profile review, request roles, and list the app in the Selling Partner Appstore with Amazon approval; private app path is distinct.
evidence.source_title: Register as a Public SP-API Developer
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The public developer guide lists approval/review requirements and describes a private-developer alternative.

evidence.claim: Production app registration requires an approved developer profile and only Amazon-approved roles can be selected.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official onboarding step requires an approved profile and role approvals before production application registration.

evidence.claim: The API surface includes many seller resource families, individual/batch/bulk operations, notifications, and a GraphQL Data Kiosk use case.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official docs enumerate resource workflow families, API access methods and Data Kiosk GraphQL.

evidence.claim: Public app access is approval/role-gated and seller authorization is required, while internal private apps follow a separate route.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Overview explains public vs private apps, Appstore approval, OAuth seller authorization and roles.

evidence.claim: Public developer registration requires external review and published app listing; restricted roles involve additional security review.
evidence.source_title: Register as a Public SP-API Developer
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official guide documents profile evaluation and review, including an architecture/security assessment for restricted roles.

limitations: MCP status was not searched in the first-pass pilot; remains UNKNOWN rather than NOT_FOUND.
No Solution Provider Portal account or seller account was used; review and credential paths are documentary.
The assignment hint points to developer docs; no precise fee/pricing claim was researched.
records.researcher_notes: A public multi-tenant integration and a private single-organization integration have different onboarding rules; keep the scope explicit.

records.description: Developer platform for building, scaling, and delivering software with code hosting and collaboration workflows.
records.self_serve_details: Users can create personal access tokens themselves; GitHub recommends GitHub Apps for organization/on-behalf-of-user integrations. Token permissions, repository ownership, org policy, and SAML SSO can limit access or require approval.

credential_access.path: Create a PAT for personal API use or register/install a GitHub App/OAuth app for delegated integrations; send the token in Authorization Bearer header.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Credential creation is self-serve for personal usage; organization policy, SAML SSO, app installation and endpoint permission requirements can restrict access.

api.details: Extensive versioned REST API documentation spans many resource families and supports integrations, data retrieval and automation; endpoint-specific token/permission requirements apply. No endpoint count used.

mcp.details: GitHub maintains the first-party github/github-mcp-server repository and hosted remote MCP server. It supports repository/code, issues/PRs and workflow tools, with PAT/OAuth/host-specific setup requirements.
mcp.search_scope: Official GitHub Docs and github/github-mcp-server first-party repository inspected.

buildability.blocker: Least-privilege token scopes/permissions, organization policy/approval, SAML SSO and app installation can limit access.
buildability.rationale: The documented REST API and official MCP server make an integration feasible now. Access is identity- and permission-bound; org-owned resources may require admin approval or installation and the MCP host/auth path varies.

evidence.claim: GitHub describes itself as a developer platform to build, scale and deliver software.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official GitHub about page describes a complete developer platform.

evidence.claim: REST API requests can use personal access tokens, GitHub App tokens, OAuth tokens, and the Authorization Bearer header; methods are token-based.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official auth page describes PAT, GitHub App and OAuth tokens and Authorization header.

evidence.claim: PATs can be created by the user; tokens inherit the user's access and can require organization-owner approval/policy.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Docs explain token creation and limits; organization owners may require approval for fine-grained PATs.

evidence.claim: Personal tokens are available for personal API use; org or long-lived integration should use GitHub Apps, with owner policy and permissions controlling access.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Page distinguishes personal token use from org app use and documents permission/policy limits.

evidence.claim: GitHub publishes a versioned REST API docs site and broad resource documentation.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official REST API documentation organizes many resource references and describes integrations, data retrieval and automation.

evidence.claim: First-party GitHub MCP server is maintained under github/github-mcp-server.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The repository is owned by github and identifies itself as GitHub official MCP Server.

evidence.claim: MCP setup uses a PAT or OAuth depending on host; tool access is limited by token permissions and org resources.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: First-party installation docs show PAT/OAuth options and token configuration.

evidence.claim: GitHub PATs are limited by user rights, scopes/permissions and organization policy; SAML SSO can require authorization.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Docs describe token permission limits, org approval policies and SAML SSO requirements.

limitations: No GitHub token or organization was used; organization-policy outcomes are documented, not account-tested.
The official MCP repository and current host support can change; the repo is a current snapshot.
records.researcher_notes: Pilot tests the distinction between self-serve personal credentials and access to an organization’s resources.

records.description: AI meeting notetaker that transcribes meetings and turns conversations into searchable summaries, insights and action items.
records.self_serve_details: The official Public API is available for Enterprise workspaces; users create an API key in account Developer settings, and accounts without the feature are directed to their account manager. MCP is a separate OAuth connection; its plan-entitlement matrix was not stated in the inspected help page.

credential_access.path: For the public API, Enterprise workspace users create a key under Integrations → Developer and send it as a Bearer token. For the first-party MCP, a supported AI host connects using OAuth/user authorization.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Public API is Enterprise-workspace only and may require account-manager enablement; MCP plan eligibility is not specified in inspected docs.

api.details: Documented REST endpoints cover channels, conversations, transcripts/audio, action items, insights, outlines and workspace data; workspace webhooks support event-triggered exports. Useful but confined to meeting/workspace data.

mcp.details: Official remote Otter MCP endpoint is https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp; OAuth-authenticated; documented tools include search, fetch and user info. Supported first-party setup paths include Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others; account/platform support can vary.
mcp.search_scope: Official Otter Help Center MCP Server page inspected, including OAuth, endpoint and tool table.

buildability.blocker: Public API is Enterprise-only; MCP tools are a bounded search/fetch/user-info surface and MCP plan/host eligibility is not fully specified.
buildability.rationale: A first-party OAuth MCP path and documented public API exist, so some agent-callable functionality is feasible. Broad API access requires Enterprise workspace availability; MCP tool coverage and host support limit scope.

evidence.claim: Otter describes itself as an AI notetaker that transcribes meetings into searchable knowledge and summaries/action items.
evidence.source_title: Otter Meeting Agent - AI Notetaker, Transcription, Insights
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official product page describes meeting transcription, searchable knowledge, summaries, insights and action items.

evidence.claim: Public API calls use a Bearer token with an API key; MCP access uses OAuth authorization.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Public API guide says all requests use Bearer token and provides API-key creation; MCP guide separately describes OAuth.

evidence.claim: The public API is available for Enterprise workspaces and may require account-manager enablement.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The getting-started section states Enterprise availability and account-manager contact if unavailable.

evidence.claim: Enterprise workspace users create API keys in Integrations → Developer; API key is limited to two keys per user.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The API guide gives the credential-generation path and Enterprise plan restriction.

evidence.claim: Public API documents REST endpoints for channels/conversations and data such as transcripts, audio, action items and insights; workspace webhooks are documented separately.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official API article describes REST endpoint groups and webhook integration.

evidence.claim: Otter documents a first-party MCP server at mcp.otter.ai/mcp with OAuth and search/fetch/user-info tools.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official help article supplies the remote MCP URL, OAuth-authenticated access and supported tool list.

evidence.claim: MCP supports bounded read/search functions while API access is Enterprise-gated, so implementation is possible but scope/access are constrained.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: MCP help page lists search, fetch and user info; public API page sets Enterprise requirement.

source_conflicts.summary: The Public API guide says Enterprise-only, while the MCP guide documents OAuth connection for supported AI apps without stating a plan gate.
source_conflicts.resolution: Classify the public API credential route as ENTERPRISE_ONLY; preserve that MCP plan eligibility is not specified instead of extending the API gate to MCP.

limitations: No Otter account or enterprise workspace was available to test API-key creation or MCP OAuth.
The API page is labeled beta in related references, and the MCP plan/host eligibility matrix is not explicit.
records.researcher_notes: Pilot intentionally includes separate API-key and OAuth MCP paths; do not collapse them into one credential requirement.
